The Firn Layer: Nature's Ice-Sheet Sponge

What it is: Firn is old, granular snow that has survived at least one summer melt season without turning to ice. It is the transitional material between fresh snow and dense glacial ice. 1. Infiltration and Refreezing: When meltwater generated at lower elevations or during warm summer events on the periphery flows or percolates into the firn, it doesn't immediately run off. Instead, it travels downward until it encounters colder temperatures at depth or until it loses heat to the surrounding snowpack, where it refreezes.
